# display server

The **Display Server** is a service that retrieves booking and reservation data for a specific tenant from the Biletado booking platform and generates HTML pages displaying upcoming reservations for specific resources (e.g., rooms, workspaces, or equipment).

These HTML pages are designed to be displayed on tablets running in kiosk mode, mounted at room entrances or directly at booked resources.

---

## Overview

The Display Server connects to a booking backend (e.g. Biletado / Smart City Booking Backend) and:

- Fetches reservations for a given tenant within a defined time range
- Groups reservations by resource
- Generates a static HTML page for each resource
- Updates the pages periodically

Typical use case:

- Tablets at room entrances
- Displays outside meeting rooms
- Resource-specific booking overview screens

The display-server is part of the **Co-Learning Spaces infrastructure of Smart City Ulm**.

## Features

- Periodically fetch bookings from the Biletado API
- Filters bookings for a defined tenant and time range
- Generates one HTML page per resource
- Optionally up to four resources can be combined on one HTML page
- Displays upcoming reservations in a clean, readable format
- Optimized for kiosk-mode display devices (e.g., tablets)
- FastAPI-based web server
- Reverse proxy compatible (BASE_PATH support)
- Optional mock backend for local development
- Deployable via Docker Compose

## Booking Platform Requirement

The display-server depends on the booking platform **smart-city-booking**, also known as **Biletado**, to retrieve reservation data.

This platform must be available before running the service, since the booking-service retrieves bookings through its API.

You can use the platform in one of the following ways:

### Option 1: Use the Hosted SaaS

The easiest way is to use the hosted version provided as SaaS by **ECC Digital**.

Website:

- <https://smart-city-booking.de/>

This option requires no infrastructure setup. You only need valid API credentials and the tenant configuration for your rooms / resources.

### Option 2: Self-Host the Platform

Alternatively, you can deploy the open source backend yourself.

Source repository:

- <https://github.com/ECCdigital/smart-city-booking-backend>

Self-hosting allows full control over the booking platform and may be preferred when operating in environments that require local infrastructure or custom integrations.

## Architecture Overview

```text
             +----------------------+
             |   Display Device     |
             | (Browser / Tablet)   |
             +----------+-----------+
                        |
                        v
               +------------------+
               |  Display Server  |
               +--------+---------+
                        |
        +---------------+---------------+
        |                               |
        v                               v
 OAuth Sign-In                  Reservation API
 Token Refresh                  (Biletado)
```

The Display Server integrates with:

- **Biletado Booking Backend**  
  Provides booking and reservation data via API

- **Display Server**  
  Processes bookings and generates static HTML output

- **Display Devices (Tablets)**  
  Load and display generated HTML pages in kiosk mode

### Dependencies

Main libraries used:
